questions.stem: Choose the incorrect statement regarding drug absorption:

options.label: B
options.text: Highly ionized molecules are absorbed from the stomach

options.label: C
options.text: Heparin is not absorbed due to its large size

options.label: D
options.text: Most common method of drug absorption is by passive diffusion

questions.answerText: Highly ionized molecules are absorbed from the stomach
questions.solutionHtml:
Highly ionized molecules are absorbed from the stomach
  • High-yield concepts about absorption
  • First-pass metabolism is inversely proportional to bioavailability, so reduces bioavailability
  • Highly ionized molecules are not at all absorbed from the stomach or intestine or any place
  • Heparin is not absorbed due to its large size and it is highly ionized
  • The most common method of drug absorption is by passive diffusion


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 17

questions.stem: A drug has a very low volume of distribution (Vd). Which of the following is the best explanation?

options.label: A
options.text: The drug is eliminated by the kidneys, and the patient has renal insufficiency

options.label: B
options.text: The drug is having a large molecular weight

options.label: C
options.text: The drug is extensively stored in tissues

options.label: D
options.text: The drug is eliminated by zero-order kinetics

questions.answerText: The drug is having a large molecular weight
questions.solutionHtml:
The drug is having a large molecular weight

Factors affecting the volume of distribution (Vd):

  • Low molecular weight drugs have high vd
  • High molecular weight drugs have low vd
  • Plasma protein binding
  • High plasma protein binding decreases vd
  • Low plasma protein binding increases vd
  • Tissue perfusion
  • Decreased tissue perfusion implies decreased vd
  • Water soluble drugs have low vd and lipid-soluble drugs have high vd
  • Tissue binding.
  • High vd with higher tissue binding

questions.stem: Following are Synthetic reactions in biotransformation except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Reduction

  • The classification of biotransformation is given by R.T.WILLIAMS
    As PHASE I and PHASE II reaction
    PHASE I Reactions:
  • Non-synthetic reaction – metabolite may be active or inactive
  • Oxidation: hydroxylation (aromatic and aliphatic)
  • Reduction
  • Hydrolysis
  • Cyclization
  • Decyclization
  • PHASE II Reactions:
    • Synthetic/Conjugation reaction – metabolite is mostly inactive
    • Glucuronidation
    • Acetylation
    • Methylation
    • Sulphate
    • Glycine
    • glutathione
  • REMEMBER:
    • PHASE I Reactions are also called Non-synthetic reaction
    • PHASE II Reactions are also called synthetic reaction

questions.answerText: Just before the next dose when the plasma concentration of the drug would be the least

Instruction given to a mother who is lactating is she should breastfeed just before the next dos, when the plasma concentration of the drug would be the least, If the nursing mother must take medications and the drug is a relatively safe one, she should optimally take it 30–60 minutes after nursing and 3–4 hours before the next feeding.

questions.stem: Loading dose depends on which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Volume of distribution
  • Loading dose of a drug is given by the formula
  • Loading dose = target plasma concentration X Volume of distribution / F
  • So from the formula it is obvious that if the volume of distribution of a drug, the loading dose also increases, for example, chloroquine has high Vd( > 13,000L), so it has to be given as a loading dose of 600mg while treating malaria

  • Note:
    • The maintenance dose of a drug is given by the formula
    • Maintenance dose = target plasma concentration X clearance X Dosing interval / F
    • so from the formula, it is obvious that the Maintenance dose depends on the clearance of the drug


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 28

questions.stem: Which of the following is incorrect about zero-order kinetics?

options.label: A
options.text: Rate of elimination of drug does not depend upon plasma concentration

options.label: B
options.text: Constant fraction of the drug is eliminated per unit of time

options.label: C
options.text: Clearance is more at low concentrations and less at high concentrations

options.label: D
options.text: Half-life is less at low concentrations and more at high concentrations.

questions.answerText: Constant fraction of the drug is eliminated per unit of time
questions.solutionHtml:
Constant fraction of the drug is eliminated per unit of time

Zero-order kinetics

  • The rate of elimination of the drug does not depend upon plasma concentration
  • A constant amount of the drug is eliminated per unit of time
  • Clearance is more at low concentrations and less at high concentrations
  • Half-life is less at low concentrations and more at high concentrations


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 38

questions.stem: Which of the following is correct regarding the mechanism of action of thyroid hormones T4 and T3 at thyroid hormone receptor?
questions.solutionHtml:
Activate nuclear transcription factor
  • T3 and T4 to act on nuclear receptors (thyroid hormone receptor).
  • By acting on these receptors they activate nuclear transcription factors
  • Both T3 and T4 penetrate cells by active transport and produce the majority of their actions by combining with a nuclear thyroid hormone receptor (TR) which belongs to the steroid and retinoid superfamily of intracellular receptors.
  • Two TR isoform families (TRα and TRβ) have been identified.


Katzung's Basic and Clinical Pharmacology- 15th Edition, chapter 38, Page Number: 9,28

questions.stem: Among the following options, the antagonism seen between heparin and protamine sulfate is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Chemical antagonism

  • Antagonism seen between heparin and protamine sulfate is Chemical antagonism
  • Heparin is a strongly negative macromolecule and protamine is a strongly positive protein. so protamine neutralizes the heparin effect by Chemical antagonism

  • Chemical antagonism:

    • The two drugs react chemically and form an inactive product,
    • E.g. KMnO4 oxidizes alkaloids—used for gastric lavage in poisoning.
    • Tannins + alkaloids—insoluble alkaloidal tannate is formed.
    • Chelating agents (BAL, Cal. disod. edetate) complex toxic metals (As, Pb).
    • Nitrites form methemoglobin which reacts with cyanide radicals.
  • Drugs may react when mixed in the same syringe or infusion bottle:

    • Thiopentone sod. + succinylcholine chloride
    • Penicillin-G sod. + succinylcholine chloride
    • Heparin + penicillin/tetracyclines/streptomycin/hydrocortison

questions.stem: A 25-year-old was suffering from gastric ulcer and he was prescribed capsule omeprazole. The pharmacogenetic analysis revealed the patient is a poor metabolizer of a CYP450 enzyme. The patient may have higher exposure to active parent drugs, a greater pharmacodynamic effect (higher gastric pH), and a higher probability of ulcer cure than heterozygotes or homozygous wild-type individuals. Which of the following enzyme does omeprazole metabolize through?
questions.solutionHtml:
CYP2C19
  • Several proton pump inhibitors, including omeprazole and lansoprazole, are inactivated by CYP2C19.
  • Thus, Poor metabolizer patients have higher exposure to active parent drugs, a greater pharmacodynamic effect (higher gastric pH), and a higher probability of ulcer cure than heterozygotes or homozygous wild-type individuals.


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No.108
